summary: Apollo is a confirmed entrant, not a rumour: it launched Olympus Housing Capital on 2025-06-30 to fund builder land acquisition and lot development, and Commercial Observer put its executed land banking at about $1 billion by July 2026. It is run by Andrew Brausa, who co-founded Domain Real Estate Partners and then built Brookfield's land financing strategies, so the new rival is led by someone who knows Domain's playbook; no public announcement from Brookfield's land financing business was found after he left. Blackstone followed in May 2026 with a BREDS homebuilder lending platform (Brio Homebuilder Solutions, 50,000-plus homes a year targeted), but nothing public says it is lot-option land banking rather than construction and land lending. Other large capital arriving in 2026: Blue Owl behind FivePoint's Hearthstone (up to $1.7 billion), Guggenheim behind Bedrock Land Finance (up to $5 billion targeted), Starwood with Trez on land A&D loans ($450 million seed, $1 billion-plus a year) and Wafra/Hunt's Strata Land Partners; Pretium has lent over $3 billion to builders but as construction-type credit. Värde still lists land banking as a live theme but has announced nothing since its April 2024 David Weekley venture. No public evidence of homebuilder land finance was found for KKR, Ares, Oaktree, Carlyle, Sixth Street, Cerberus, Centerbridge, Bain, Fortress (beyond a 2022 Walton facility), PIMCO, Goldman Sachs AM, Invesco, Rockpoint or Pacific Life, though several of those got only a light check because the search budget ran out.

facts.fact: Apollo: on 2025-06-30 Apollo announced Olympus Housing Capital, an Apollo affiliate and new homebuilder finance strategy that funds land acquisition and the development work that turns entitled residential land into finished lots, for both public and private builders. The release names no fund size, product names or builder customers.
facts.source_title: Apollo press release: Apollo Announces Olympus Housing Capital (2025-06-30)

facts.fact: Apollo: Olympus Housing Capital originations are funded by Apollo-managed funds and affiliated balance sheets, per the launch release. The release does not name Athene as the funding source (Athene appears only in Apollo's standard company description), so an Athene link is not publicly stated.
facts.source_title: Apollo press release: Apollo Announces Olympus Housing Capital (2025-06-30)

facts.fact: Apollo: Commercial Observer's 2026 Power Investors profile of Apollo real estate equity head Bert Crouch (published 2026-07-30) says Apollo has executed about $1 billion of land banking through Olympus Housing Capital, roughly 13 months after launch. The same profile notes Apollo's private equity business owns top-25 builder Risewell Homes and that Apollo is in advanced talks to add a build-to-rent vertical. No builders, lot counts or yields are given.
facts.source_title: Commercial Observer, Power Investors 2026: Bert Crouch (2026-07-30)

facts.fact: Apollo: Olympus Housing Capital is led by CEO Andrew Brausa, who joined Apollo in March 2025. Before Apollo he set up and ran Brookfield Asset Management's land financing strategies, and earlier co-founded Domain Real Estate Partners and managed public-market portfolios at DW Partners. Apollo partners Peter Sinensky and Nancy de Liban sponsored the launch.
facts.source_title: IPE Real Assets: Brausa to lead Apollo's newly formed US homebuilder finance company (2025-06-30)

facts.fact: Blackstone: on 2026-05-11 Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies (BREDS) announced a homebuilder lending platform expected to support construction of more than 50,000 for-sale homes a year, run through BREDS portfolio company Brio Homebuilder Solutions plus unnamed third-party partners. Coverage describes multi-year programmatic builder relationships but does not say whether the product is land banking, land/lot loans or construction loans; no dollar size or builder names were given.
facts.source_title: HousingWire: Blackstone homebuilder lending platform (2026-05-11)

facts.fact: Blackstone: Commercial Observer (2026-06-01) reports Blackstone told it BREDS, which it describes as a $78 billion real estate debt platform, had already been lending on for-sale home construction for nearly a year before the May 2026 announcement, that the total financing amount is still to be determined, and that this is a first-of-its-kind initiative for the firm. The article does not mention land banking or lot options.
facts.source_title: Commercial Observer: Behind Blackstone's Newfound Commitment to Finance Home Construction (2026-06-01)

facts.fact: Blackstone: the homebuilder lending platform was announced by Tim Johnson, global head of BREDS. A search-result snippet of The Real Deal's 2026-05-11 coverage names Robert Maddox as CEO of Brio Homebuilder Solutions, but that page would not open (HTTP 403), so the Brio CEO name is seen in a snippet only.
facts.source_title: IREI: Blackstone Real Estate Debt Strategies launches homebuilder lending platform (2026-05-11)

facts.fact: Starwood: on 2026-11-03 Starwood Capital Group and Trez Capital announced a partnership to originate residential land acquisition-and-development (A&D) loans for single-family communities across the US, seeded with a $450 million portfolio of US residential land A&D loans originated by Trez and targeting more than $1 billion of originations a year. It is horizontal development lending, not lot-option land banking; loan sizes, pricing and borrowers were not disclosed.
facts.source_title: HousingWire: Starwood / Trez Capital residential land lending (2026-11-06)

facts.fact: Starwood: the Starwood-Trez land lending partnership was announced by Anthony Murphy, managing director at Starwood Capital, with Trez Capital co-CEOs John D. Hutchinson (global head of origination) and John Maragliano (CFO). Bisnow notes Starwood had earlier bought several Texas master-planned communities from Hines (an $800 million deal) in which Trez had been Hines's partner.
facts.source_title: Bisnow: Starwood Launches Residential Land JV Targeting $1B In Annual Originations (2026-11-03)

facts.fact: Pretium: Pretium closed its first homebuilder finance fund with $550 million of equity commitments in January 2025, aiming to originate up to $5 billion of loans to US homebuilders by recycling capital over the fund's life.
facts.source_title: Alternatives Watch: Pretium launches $550 million homebuilder finance fund (2025-01-16)

facts.fact: Pretium: by 2026-05-07 Pretium said it had passed $3 billion of residential lending since its December 2024 platform launch, supporting more than 13,000 housing units, across single-family for-sale and rental construction and multifamily. It targets mid-sized builders producing 200 to 2,000 homes a year and originates with its affiliate Anchor Loans. The coverage describes construction-type lending and does not mention land banking or lot options.
facts.source_title: Pulse 2.0: Pretium Surpasses $3 Billion In Financing To Homebuilders And Multifamily Developers (2026-05-07)

facts.fact: Värde Partners: Värde's real estate strategy page (retrieved 2026-11-19) still lists land banking partnerships that finance the creation of residential lots for sale to homebuilders as a current capital-solutions theme. It gives only firm-wide real estate figures ($24 billion-plus invested, 415-plus investments, 15 investment professionals) and no named platform, dollar size, lot count or builder list for land banking.
facts.source_title: Värde Partners website: Real Estate strategy page (retrieved 2026-11-19)

facts.fact: Värde Partners: the last land-banking announcement found on Värde's own site is the 2024-04-04 joint venture with David Weekley Homes (Värde provides the land banking facility, David Weekley sources and develops), which had closed two Phoenix projects with over $100 million of project costs and targeted Phoenix, Tampa, Atlanta, Orlando and Charlotte. Facility size was not disclosed. This is older than 24 months with no newer public confirmation, hence Inferred as to current status.
facts.source_title: Värde press release: Värde Partners and David Weekley Homes Announce Land Banking Joint Venture (2024-04-04)

facts.fact: Värde Partners: no 2025-2026 land-banking or homebuilder announcement found. The ten most recent items on Värde's announcements page (2026-02-06 to 2026-09-30) are CRE loans, a $1 billion CRE CLO, European financings and awards; the closest is a $65.5 million refinancing of a Phoenix build-to-rent community (2026-09-30). Searches for 'Värde land banking 2026', 'Värde homebuilder finance platform' and 'Värde homebuilder joint venture 2025 OR 2026' returned only the 2021-2024 Taylor Morrison, Dream Finders, American Homes 4 Rent and David Weekley deals. Inferred from absence.
facts.source_title: Värde Partners website: Announcements index, page 1 (retrieved 2026-11-19)

facts.fact: Brookfield: Brookfield Residential's land website (retrieved 2026-11-19, footer copyright 2024) markets a 'Land Banking' offering that gives homebuilders structured, stable capital for balance-sheet flexibility, but discloses no deal terms, capital amount, builders or lot counts (its 'Managed Lots' and 'Active Land Banks' counters display zero, apparently unpopulated).
facts.source_title: Brookfield Residential Land website (retrieved 2026-11-19)

facts.fact: Brookfield: the executive who founded and ran Brookfield Asset Management's land financing strategies, Andrew Brausa, left and joined Apollo in March 2025 to head Olympus Housing Capital. No public announcement of a successor or of a dedicated Brookfield land-bank fund in 2025-2026 was found (searches: 'Brookfield land financing strategy homebuilders 2025 2026', 'Brookfield Residential lot banking 2026').
facts.source_title: IPE Real Assets: Brausa to lead Apollo's newly formed US homebuilder finance company (2025-06-30)

facts.fact: Brookfield: the only sized public reference found to Brookfield's lot-banking ambitions is a PERE teaser dated 2021-06-09 saying that, through its Newland acquisition, Brookfield had control of over 80,000 lots and wanted to bring scale to residential lot banking (article body paywalled). Older than 24 months with no newer confirmation, hence Inferred.
facts.source_title: PERE: Why Brookfield wants to bring scale to residential lot banking (2021-06-09, teaser only)

facts.fact: Blue Owl (name surfaced by search): on 2026-02-10 Five Point Holdings announced that its Hearthstone land-banking platform had formed a residential land banking investment partnership with funds managed by Blue Owl Capital to buy residential homesites and land for national homebuilders. Five Point issued Blue Owl funds warrants at $7.00 per share that vest as cumulative capital contributions hit set thresholds (about 1% dilution if fully exercised). The release gives no dollar size.
facts.source_title: Five Point Holdings press release: new Hearthstone residential land banking investment partnership with Blue Owl managed funds (2026-02-10)

facts.fact: Blue Owl (name surfaced by search): the Orange County Business Journal (2026-03-02) reports the Hearthstone-Blue Owl partnership could buy up to $1.7 billion of US residential land, with Blue Owl's warrants vesting from $500 million of contributed capital up to $1.7 billion. It reports Hearthstone's assets under management at about $3.4 billion (up from about $2.6 billion when FivePoint bought 75% of it in 2025) and that FivePoint expected $300-500 million of new capital commitments in Q1 2026. The $1.7 billion is a ceiling, not committed capital.
facts.source_title: Orange County Business Journal: FivePoint and Blue Owl launch $1.7B deal (2026-03-02)

facts.fact: Guggenheim (name surfaced by search): Guggenheim Investments' own news page announces a land banking finance platform that provides land banking financing to homebuilders in high-growth markets through a relationship with Bedrock Land Finance, a residential land development originator and servicer. The page says Bedrock has active projects covering more than 7,500 single-family lots nationally and works with many of the leading public homebuilders; it names no builders, dollar target or capital source. The page itself is undated; trade coverage dates the announcement to 2026-05-19/21.
facts.source_title: Guggenheim Investments: Expands Real Estate Capabilities with Land Banking Finance Platform (2026-05-19)

facts.fact: Guggenheim (name surfaced by search): IREI (2026-05-21) reports Bedrock Land Finance, a land banking and A&D lender to homebuilders whose parent is TWG Global, was named exclusive land banking partner for the Guggenheim Investments Land Banking Strategy; it describes Guggenheim as having more than $362 billion of total assets. Only the opening of the article is free.
facts.source_title: IREI: Bedrock named exclusive land banking partner for Guggenheim Investments (2026-05-21)

facts.fact: Guggenheim (name surfaced by search): CRE Daily (2026-05-28) reports that Bedrock Land Finance, Guggenheim Investments' land-banking partner, plans to fund up to $5 billion of residential development projects over the coming years; treat that as a target, not committed capital. A search snippet of the press release (not opened, so unconfirmed) adds that Bedrock had already committed over $1 billion to 16 builders and developers.
facts.source_title: CRE Daily: PGIM Bets Big on Land Banking as Homebuilders Seek Flexibility (2026-05-28)

facts.fact: Wafra / Hunt Companies (name surfaced by search): Strata Land Partners launched in early November 2026, backed by Wafra (about $30 billion AUM) and Hunt Companies, to provide land financing and lot-development capital to public and private builders nationwide, with a mandate described as broader than traditional land banking. It starts with projects totalling about 1,300 single-family lots and is led by Michael Forsum, former Landsea Homes president and COO and a Starwood Land Ventures alumnus. Capital commitment and builder customers were not disclosed.
facts.source_title: The Builder's Daily / HousingWire: Strata Land Partners launch (2026-11-02)

facts.fact: Avila Real Estate Capital (name surfaced by search; builder-backed lender rather than a large alternative manager): AREC's second debt fund reached about $200 million of commitments toward a $1 billion target at its second close (reported 2026-03-09), anchored by Hillwood Communities, with D.R. Horton, Toll Brothers and Century Communities investing as limited partners. It lends land development and AD&C capital to developers and private builders and aims to originate about $1 billion a year.
facts.source_title: The Builder's Daily / HousingWire: Horton, Toll, Century back AREC Fund as AD&C credit tightens (2026-03-09)

facts.fact: Apollo: Olympus Housing Capital's own website (retrieved 2026-11-19) describes itself as an Apollo affiliate with access to long-duration capital, offering financing for residential land acquisition and development (planning and engineering through utilities, roads and amenities), customized investment structures and an 'off-balance sheet homesite supply' for homebuilders, with post-closing asset management. That is land-banking language, though the site never uses the words 'land banking' and lists no capital deployed, lots, offices or builder customers.
facts.source_title: Olympus Housing Capital website (retrieved 2026-11-19)

facts.fact: Apollo: Olympus Housing Capital's website lists an 11-person leadership roster under CEO Andrew Brausa, including Senior Vice Presidents Aimee Martin and Troy Wahlberg, Controller Alexa Brennan, Associate Vice Presidents Matt Caldwell and Donna Ransom (Closings), four senior associates and one associate. Headcount is a count of the names shown on the page on 2026-11-19 (the page was truncated, so the list may be incomplete).
facts.source_title: Olympus Housing Capital website (retrieved 2026-11-19)

facts.fact: Apollo: Apollo is also a land-bank customer through its builder. Apollo funds have been majority shareholder of The New Home Company (carried as Risewell Homes in the Builder 100 list, the name Commercial Observer also uses for Apollo's builder) since 2021 and committed $650 million of new equity to its all-cash acquisition of Landsea Homes ($11.30 a share, about $1.2 billion, announced May 2025), with Millrose Properties buying select Landsea land and optioning it back to the combined builder. The article calls Millrose a land banking affiliate of Apollo; that wording conflicts with Millrose's public status as a Lennar spin-off externally managed by Kennedy Lewis, so read it as loose trade-press phrasing rather than an ownership fact.
facts.source_title: The Builder's Daily / HousingWire: New Home-Landsea Deal Redraws Builder Power Map (2025-05-13)

facts.fact: Fortress: no public evidence of land banking or homebuilder land finance found in 2025-2026 after searching 'Sixth Street OR Cerberus OR Fortress OR Carlyle homebuilder land financing lots builder facility announced 2026' and 'Pretium OR Bain Capital OR Fortress homebuilder land banking OR finished lots OR builder finance facility 2025 2026'. The only link found is old: on 2022-06-02 affiliates of Fortress-managed funds provided a $100 million facility (expandable to $150 million) to Walton Global's builder land financing business. Inferred from absence.
facts.source_title: Walton Global press release: $100 Million Builder Land Financing with Fortress Investment Group (2022-06-02)

facts.fact: Oaktree: no public evidence of land banking or homebuilder land finance found in 2025-2026 after searching 'Oaktree Capital homebuilder land banking lots financing builder 2025 2026' and 'KKR OR Ares OR Oaktree land banking homebuilder facility 2025 2026'. Its visible homebuilding exposure is ownership: single-lot builder Thomas James Homes is backed by Oaktree-managed funds (IREI, 2026-08-10). Inferred from absence.
facts.source_title: IREI: Oaktree-backed Thomas James Homes (2026-08-10, opening only; rest paywalled)

facts.fact: Brookfield: Warren Krug is chief investment officer of Brookfield Residential and was quoted on 2026-10-16 saying large 2026 housing deals are replacing shorter-term private-equity capital with longer-dated owners; the same article cites Brookfield's Newland and Kolter transactions as examples of investing in land operators before buying them. The article does not describe a Brookfield land-bank fund.
facts.source_title: The Builder's Daily / HousingWire: Housing M&A shifts as global capital retargets residential futures (2026-10-16)

facts.fact: PGIM / insurance capital (reader's own partner, included because insurance capital was on the checklist): CRE Daily (2026-05-28) reports Prudential Financial's asset-management arm has backed roughly $4 billion of residential land-bank deals and completed seven transactions through a partnership with Domain Real Estate Partners begun in 2025. No Pacific Life land-banking activity surfaced in any search.
facts.source_title: CRE Daily: PGIM Bets Big on Land Banking as Homebuilders Seek Flexibility (2026-05-28)

facts.fact: Market context for entrants (not firm-specific): a June 2025 HousingWire column by Scott Cox of SLC Advisors says new land-bank funds typically charge builders about 11%, run roughly 45% leverage at about SOFR plus 200 basis points and so reach mid-teens returns on equity, and calls Millrose's 8.5% pooled rate to Lennar (about 7% after management fees) exceptionally low and a level that could push other participants out.
facts.source_title: HousingWire: Understanding homebuilding's new capital partner, land banking, by Scott Cox (2025-06-04)

facts.fact: Market context for entrants (not firm-specific): The Builder's Daily (2026-10-16) reports that Essential Housing's land-bank arrangements typically cost builders 200 to 250 basis points above their blended cost of capital, and that Essential Housing has originated over $22 billion of land-bank investments in five years and is raising capital for about $10 billion more.
facts.source_title: The Builder's Daily / HousingWire: Housing M&A shifts as global capital retargets residential futures (2026-10-16)

gaps: Apollo / Olympus Housing Capital: fund size, named builder customers, lot counts, option-fee yields and whether Athene is the balance sheet are not publicly disclosed (Apollo release, IPE, Commercial Observer checked). olympushc.com could not be opened (WebFetch domain check rate-limited).

Blackstone: the primary press release on blackstone.com returned a bot-check page and the BusinessWire and The Real Deal copies returned HTTP 403, so Blackstone rows rest on trade-press copies (IREI, HousingWire, Commercial Observer). Product mix (land banking vs land loans vs construction loans), dollar size, Brio Homebuilder Solutions leadership and builder names are not public in what could be opened.

Värde Partners: current platform name, size, lot count and builder list for its land-banking business are not publicly disclosed. Värde's site names no branded homebuilder-finance platform; the last announced deals are David Weekley (2024-04), American Homes 4 Rent ($500 million, 2022), Taylor Morrison (over $1 billion, 2021) and Dream Finders ($100 million, seen in search results only). Whether those facilities are still drawing in 2026 could not be confirmed from free sources.

Brookfield: no 2025-2026 press release, fund name, size or builder list for Brookfield's land financing / lot banking was found, and no successor to Andrew Brausa was identified. brookfield.com would not load (domain check rate-limited, then 404 on the one URL tried); the PERE 2021 article is paywalled.

KKR: no public evidence of US homebuilder land banking or land finance in 2025-2026 (searches: 'KKR OR Ares OR Oaktree land banking homebuilder facility 2025 2026'; 'KKR homebuilder land financing lots land bank builder 2026'). Only a UK living-sector lending JV with Puma (GBP 500 million, March 2026) appeared in a search snippet; nothing citable was opened.

Ares: no public evidence of homebuilder land banking or land finance in 2025-2026 (searches: 'Ares Management residential land lot banking homebuilder land banking'; the combined KKR/Ares/Oaktree queries). Only a 2010 equity investment in builder City Ventures surfaced; nothing citable was opened.

Carlyle, Sixth Street, Cerberus, Centerbridge: no public evidence of homebuilder land banking or land finance in 2025-2026 (searches: 'Carlyle OR Sixth Street OR Cerberus OR Centerbridge homebuilder land banking OR lot option OR land finance 2025 2026'; 'Sixth Street OR Cerberus OR Fortress OR Carlyle homebuilder land financing lots builder facility announced 2026'). Results were unrelated (a Carlyle/Sixth Street BDC CLO venture, a Centerbridge commercial property stake). No firm-specific page was opened, and planned one-firm follow-up searches could not be run because the shared web-search budget ran out.

Bain Capital: no public evidence found (search: 'Pretium OR Bain Capital OR Fortress homebuilder land banking OR finished lots OR builder finance facility 2025 2026'); the single-firm follow-up search was blocked by the search budget, so this is a light check.

PIMCO, Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Invesco, Rockpoint: no public evidence found (search: 'Goldman Sachs OR Invesco OR Rockpoint OR PIMCO land banking homebuilder 2025 2026'); results returned only PGIM, Guggenheim and general market pieces.
